lessons.title: Classes and Objects
lessons.concept: Object-Oriented Programming (OOP) organizes code around objects that combine data (attributes/fields) and behavior (methods). A class is a blueprint/template that defines the structure and behavior, while an object is an instance created from that class.
lessons.formula: Class defines attributes + methods; Object = instance of a class with specific state.
lessons.worked_example: A 'Car' class may define attributes like color and speed and methods like accelerate(). An object car1 might be a red Car instance with speed 0 initially.
mistakes: Confusing a class (blueprint) with an object (instance)
Thinking methods exist without being associated with class/object behavior
Assuming all objects of a class must have identical attribute values

lessons.title: Encapsulation and Abstraction
lessons.concept: Encapsulation bundles data and methods together and restricts direct access to some of an object's components (often via access control), helping protect internal state. Abstraction hides complex implementation details and exposes only essential features/interfaces.
lessons.formula: Encapsulation: data + methods + controlled access. Abstraction: expose 'what' an object does, hide 'how' it does it.
lessons.worked_example: A BankAccount class may keep balance private and provide deposit()/withdraw() methods. Users interact with these methods without directly modifying internal balance representation details.
mistakes: Treating encapsulation and abstraction as identical concepts
Assuming encapsulation means data must never be accessed (it means controlled access)
Exposing internal implementation unnecessarily, breaking abstraction

lessons.title: Inheritance and Polymorphism
lessons.concept: Inheritance allows a class (child/subclass) to derive properties and behavior from another class (parent/superclass), promoting reuse. Polymorphism allows entities to take multiple forms, commonly method overriding (same method name, different behavior in subclasses) or method overloading (same name, different parameters, language-dependent).
lessons.formula: Inheritance: subclass extends superclass. Polymorphism: one interface/name, multiple behaviors/forms.
lessons.worked_example: A base class Shape may define area(); subclasses Circle and Rectangle implement area() differently. Calling area() on a Shape reference can invoke the appropriate subclass implementation (runtime polymorphism in many languages).
mistakes: Assuming inheritance is always the best way to reuse code
Expecting child classes to automatically change parent private implementation details

practice.question: In OOP, what is a class?
practice.explanation: A class defines the attributes and methods that its objects will have; it serves as a blueprint for creating instances (objects).

practice.explanation: An object is a concrete instance created from a class, having its own state (attribute values) and access to behaviors (methods).
